source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 3 (ISL A3) · lesson 8. Rewritten for children from Dr. Hassan's lesson; facts and references kept.
topic: Five prayers that wash us clean

learn.en: Ṣalāh is the second pillar of Islam, right after the shahādah. Allah made five prayers a day, each at its own time. (Qur'an 4:103)
learn.title: Five a day

learn.en: The Prophet ﷺ asked: if a river ran by your door and you bathed in it five times a day, would any dirt stay on you? “That is like the five prayers; Allah wipes away sins with them.” (Bukhari 528)
learn.title: A river at your door

learn.en: Prayer keeps us away from bad things: “Indeed, prayer stops shameful and wrong deeds.” (Qur'an 29:45)
learn.title: It keeps us good

learn.en: Praying together in jamāʿah is 27 times better than praying alone. (Bukhari 645)
learn.title: 27 times better

learn.en: We never stop praying — at home or travelling, healthy or ill. If you can't stand, pray sitting; if you can't sit, pray on your side. (Bukhari 1117)
learn.title: Never dropped

order.en: Put the five prayers in order

quiz.en: Which pillar of Islam is ṣalāh?
Praying in jamāʿah is how many times better?
What does an ill person do if he cannot stand?
True or false? The five prayers wash away sins like a river washes dirt.

think.q: Which prayer is the hardest for you to pray on time? What is one thing you can do to protect it?
think.a: Maybe an alarm for Fajr, or praying Asr as soon as you get home — small steps keep the prayer safe.

parents.summary: Ṣalāh is the second pillar: five prayers at set times that wash away sins and keep us from wrong. Praying together is 27 times better, and we never drop it.
parents.tip: Choose one prayer this week to pray together as a family every day.
